correctness.rationale: Read final RESULT.md and source verify programs. Substituting identities in the group RB law forces B(1)=1 and B(z) in {1,z} for the unique central involution z. The auxiliary group law g∘h=gB(g)hB(g)^(−1) makes B and C(g)=gB(g) homomorphisms, while its Q/Z projection agrees with ordinary multiplication. If B(z)=1, B descends from elementary abelian Q/Z and hence has central image χ; if B(z)=z, C descends similarly, yielding B(g)=g^(−1)χ(g). Each of four characters gives a valid map in each family; disjointness follows from B(z). Character orbits under Aut(Q8), duality, splitting subgroup obstruction and bijectivity are verified. Independent multiplication-table checks tested all eight maps on all 64 (g,h) pairs and confirmed images and duals, though not the full independent 8^7 enumeration claimed by the source.
